disclaimer: Fees and rules change, sometimes mid-season. Treat these as a planning guide and confirm with the Nepal Tourism Board, the Department of Immigration or a registered agency before you travel.

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.authority: Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.
permits.notes: Children under 10 enter free. Nepali press reports from 2024 to 2026 give the same NPR 3,000, 1,500 and 100. Whether 13% VAT is added for foreigners is disputed: an independent guide says tax has been folded into park fees since 2019, while several agency sites still quote NPR 3,390. We found no official statement, so carry the difference in cash. Keep the permit handy; it is checked at the gate.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.
permits.notes: The municipality calls it a Trek Card: staff take your passport details and a photo, which takes about 15 minutes. It has stood in for the TIMS card in Khumbu since October 2017, when the fee was NPR 2,000. The municipality's own page now lists NPR 3,000, with NPR 2,000 for SAARC and Chinese passport holders, and its 2024–25 visitor and revenue figures fit that split. A few agency pages say every foreigner pays NPR 3,000. Bring rupees in cash.

permits.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site, or in person at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, and the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.
permits.notes: The fee includes tax and children under 10 do not need a permit. Paying online by card adds a 2.9% gateway charge. Covers every trek in the Annapurna range and Lower Mustang; Upper Mustang and Nar Phu need a restricted-area permit as well.

permits.name: Manaslu Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site or at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu. In practice your agency arranges it with the restricted-area permit.
permits.notes: The fee includes tax and children under 10 do not need a permit. The Manaslu circuit finishes inside the Annapurna Conservation Area, so you need an ACAP as well.

permits.name: Langtang National Park entry permit
permits.authority: Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation
permits.where: At the park checkpoint in Dhunche on the drive to Syabrubesi, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.
permits.notes: The Nepal Tourism Board and current guides agree on NPR 3,000 and NPR 1,500. Some agencies add 13% VAT to the foreigner fee (NPR 3,390); we could not confirm that it is charged, so carry the difference. NPR 100 for Nepali citizens is the standard mountain-park rate; the tourism board's page still shows an older figure.

permits.authority: Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation
permits.where: Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, or the park entry posts at Num and Seduwa on the trail.
permits.notes: Children under 10 are exempt. All three rates match the Nepal Tourism Board's current fee table; whether VAT is added on top is unconfirmed. permits.name: Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, normally arranged by your agency with the restricted-area permit. Foreign trekkers are also registered at check posts on the trail, for example at Ghunsa.
permits.notes: NPR 2,000 for foreigners, NPR 500 for SAARC nationals and NPR 100 for Nepali citizens are the figures in the Nepal Tourism Board's current fee table; children under 10 are free. A few agency pages list NPR 3,000, which is the NTNC rate and does not apply here, because this area is run by a local council under the Department of National Parks.

permits.name: Khaptad National Park entry permit
permits.authority: Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation
permits.where: At the park entry post on the way in, or in advance at the national parks counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.
permits.notes: NPR 3,000 for foreigners, NPR 1,500 for SAARC nationals and NPR 100 for Nepali citizens are the figures in the Nepal Tourism Board's current fee table, which it says follows the parks department; children under 10 are free. Budget for the higher, current figure, carry a margin for tax, and ask at the park office if you are charged differently.

permits.name: Api Nampa Conservation Area Permit
permits.authority: Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation
permits.where: At the conservation area office in Darchula, or in advance at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu, where your agency can arrange it.
permits.notes: The Nepal Tourism Board's current park fee table, which it says follows the parks department, lists NPR 2,000 for foreigners, NPR 500 for SAARC nationals and NPR 100 for Nepali citizens, with children under 10 free. Most 2025–26 agency lists give the same foreigner and SAARC rates. Older pages that show NPR 1,000 or NPR 3,000 plus VAT do not match it. The department's own website carried no fee table when we checked on 22 November 2026, and whether VAT is added is unconfirmed, so carry a small margin. The Byas valley towards the border needs the Darchula restricted-area permit as well.

permits.name: Trekkers' Information Management System card
permits.authority: Nepal Tourism Board and the Trekking Agencies' Association of Nepal
permits.where: Only through a registered trekking agency, which applies in the Nepal Tourism Board's online system with your route and your guide's details. Individual trekkers can no longer buy one over the counter.
permits.notes: Since the revised rules of 31 March 2023 the card is tied to trekking with a licensed guide on the tourism board's listed routes. It is not used in Khumbu, where the municipality's Trek Card took its place in 2017. For restricted areas the published rules pull both ways: TAAN's pages say TIMS applies in every trekking area, restricted ones included, yet also list visitors holding Department of Immigration permits among those who do not need one, and agencies disagree. Your agency, which is compulsory there anyway, will know what the checkposts on your route ask for. Reports from 2025–26 describe patchy checks of the card, especially in Annapurna.

permits.name: Upper Mustang restricted area permit
permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu (the Pokhara immigration office also issues them), through a registered trekking agency only.
permits.notes: The old flat fee of USD 500 for ten days was scrapped by a cabinet decision in November 2025. The Department of Immigration's fee table now shows USD 50 a day with no minimum stay, so a ten-day trip costs the same and a shorter one costs less. Since 22 March 2026 the permit can be issued to a single trekker, but you still need a registered agency and a licensed guide (at most seven trekkers per guide). The permit is checked at Kagbeni, and you need an ACAP as well.

permits.name: Upper Dolpo restricted area permit
permits.where: Department of Immigration in Kathmandu, through a registered trekking agency only.
permits.notes: The Nepal Tourism Board's permit fee table now lists Upper Dolpo at USD 50 a person a day, the same as Upper Mustang, in place of the old USD 500 for the first ten days. For a stay of ten days the cost is unchanged; a shorter crossing costs less and a longer one costs USD 50 for every extra day. Since 22 March 2026 the permit can be issued to a single trekker, but you still need a registered agency and a licensed guide (at most seven trekkers per guide). The Shey Phoksundo park permit and the Lower Dolpo permit for the approach are extra. Ask your agency to count the days you will spend inside the restricted area.
